items.note: Sources: two MedStation WhatsApp sessions on 9/2 (01M1H7CF, 01M1HW6C) plus the Medstation GoHighLevel and Medstation Marketing chats on 9/1. New fact this run: the Weston migration is blocked by a WhatsApp platform limit of one active number per business account, with no dual number setting in the Android app, so this needs a route decision rather than more configuration. Board audit 9/3 across all four boards with subitems: no WhatsApp item or subitem exists on CRM, Ads, Video or Web + SEO. The former parent GHL Setup (12665521507) is no longer on the CRM board and its old children (Weston Pilot, Review Engine, Reactivation Build, Phone Consolidation, Lead Escalation) are now top level MedStation items, so create_item in the MedStation group is the correct shape rather than create_subitem. Section 19b: no match against any non terminal card. The completed medstation-whatsapp-ghl-connect card is terminal and was deliberately not reopened. blocked true because the Meta Business Manager payment removal sits with MedStation; needsNaz true because this gates the pilot and needs a spend and device decision.

payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context. Weston's WhatsApp number is the last open gate before the MedStation GoHighLevel pilot can run. On 1 September the number was connected into GHL through Lead Connector by QR scan, then a shared payment method on the WhatsApp Business account blocked data flow, so the plan became to move Weston onto its own WhatsApp Business account. Jonatan Herculano on the MedStation side agreed to remove the card from that account inside Meta Business Manager. Renata Barros holds the handset and has been doing the scans.
  • What the 2 September sessions found, and this is the new part. The migration is blocked by a platform limit, not a configuration mistake. A WhatsApp Business account accepts only one active number, and the Android app in use exposes no advanced or dual number setting, so there is no way to add Weston as a second number on the existing account and no way to run both from the same handset. Creating and linking a fresh business account also threw errors that were not resolved on the call. The team wants to keep the current phone in service, which is what makes this a decision rather than a build.
  • Deliverable, step one. Write up the routes that actually clear the one number limit, with what each costs MedStation in money, time and disruption. The realistic set is a dedicated handset for the Weston number, moving Weston onto the WhatsApp Business Platform through a provider number instead of the phone app, or keeping the shared account and removing the payment conflict so both clinics stay on one number. Say which one you recommend and why.
  • Deliverable, step two. Once a route is chosen, connect Weston into GHL on it and prove it with a live two way message test, inbound and outbound, logged against a real GHL contact. Do not start step two before step one is signed off, because each route puts the number on a different account and undoing that is manual.
  • Dependencies. Removing the payment method from the Weston WhatsApp account inside Meta Business Manager sits with Jonatan Herculano at MedStation and was still open at the end of 1 September. Renata Barros is the person with the handset for any scan. Sohib is running the account work directly on the client calls, so coordinate through him rather than contacting the clinic separately.
  • Constraints. Do not take the currently working WhatsApp number out of service while testing, and do not move the other MedStation locations onto a new account as part of this. Weston only, the same separation the pilot already assumes.
  • done = Weston sends and receives WhatsApp through GHL on an account that shares neither a number nor a payment method with another clinic, a live two way test is recorded here, and the chosen route is written down so the remaining locations can follow it.

Sharif Maadi updated the Maadi Law billing details on 1 September, so that account is current.
